title: Mechanism of the long-B prokaryotic Argonaute-mediated nuclease activation in bacterial immunity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unpacked the Europe PMC supplement zip (7.6 MB) and fully parsed the 30 MB Word supplement: it contains 4 tables (101 table rows total) - Table S1 = 2 protein sequences (EcAgo, EcbAgaN), Table S2 = 37 plasmid names, Table S3 = 31 oligonucleotide sequences, Table S4 = cryo-EM collection statistics. Confirmed the two deposited files are live: HEAD on https://files.rcsb.org/download/23WQ.cif.gz returned HTTP 200, 1,909,368 bytes, and the EMDB API returned metadata for EMD-69324. No CSV, TSV or XLSX file exists anywhere in the paper's data.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: All quantitative results (percent DNA cleavage per mutant, efficiency of plaquing against 6 phages, mismatch-position tolerance, growth curves) are described in text and shown as gel photographs and bar charts inside the figures; I read the figure captions but no numeric values are tabulated anywhere I could open.

a1_downloadable.note: Pass, verified: PDB entry 23WQ downloads (HTTP 200, 1.9 MB mmCIF) and EMDB EMD-69324 metadata resolves; supplement opens without a login.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no label column anywhere. Every possible outcome (cleavage activity, plaque-forming efficiency, mismatch tolerance) exists only as a gel image or bar chart inside a Word document, so the target would have to be constructed by eyeballing or digitising figures.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs as such are present: two full amino-acid sequences and 31 guide-RNA/target-DNA oligonucleotide sequences are typed out in Tables S1 and S3; but they describe one system, not a dataset.

a4_units_stated.note: No quantitative data table exists, so there is nothing with units; bar-chart axes in figures are the only place any quantity appears.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL badly. Counted in the files: 37 plasmid constructs (mutants), 31 oligonucleotides, 21 single-mismatch target variants, 6 phages, 1 structure. Checklist floor is ~400 rows for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; the problem is that there is almost nothing to load.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Table counts I extracted (37 plasmids, 31 oligos, 309,746 cryo-EM particles, 21,538 micrographs) are internally consistent with the methods text.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not applicable - no label exists. The measurements that do exist are genuine wet-lab gels, not model outputs, so there is no circularity problem, just no data table.

existing_models.name: DefensePredictor (Science, 2025) - gradient-boosting classifier on protein language model embeddings that flags bacterial anti-phage defence proteins
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported average precision 0.95 on its held-out test set; applied to 69 Escherichia coli strains and 1,000 prokaryotic genomes, with 42 predictions experimentally validated (numbers from the search result summaries, not from re-running the model).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: They report ~3,000 protein clusters with no homology to known systems, i.e. mechanism and partner-gene assignment for novel candidates remains open.

integration.partner_dataset: none worth naming for a single structure; the sequences could be joined to UniProt/AlphaFold DB, but two proteins is not a join
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written from this paper's data alone.

controls.positive_control: none definable - no dataset to recover a known signal from

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim is possible: this paper reports one cryo-EM structure and gel-based assays on one bacterial immune system, which supports mechanistic conclusions but cannot support a trained predictor.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein and guide sequences to predict how strongly a bacterial Argonaute defence complex cuts DNA (considered, then rejected).
plain_idea.train_on: The only candidate training examples are 37 mutant protein constructs and 21 single-mismatch DNA targets, read off gel images; verified counts from the supplementary tables.
plain_idea.predict: Cleavage activity or anti-phage plaque reduction, which were measured by gel electrophoresis and plaque assays and reported only as pictures and bar charts, never as numbers in a file.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Nothing could be learned at this scale - any model on ~37 hand-digitised points would be curve-fitting; the structure itself is still valuable to structural biologists as a mechanism, just not as machine-learning data.

more_or_better_data.why: This paper contributes one structure and ~37 mutant assays; DefensePredictor was trained on genome-scale protein sets across 1,000 prokaryotic genomes.

confidence_score.why: Triplicate error bars exist in figures but only as images, so no per-prediction uncertainty could be derived.

models_beatable.why: DefensePredictor is a 2025 protein-language-model-based classifier with open code and experimental validation of 42 predictions; nothing here competes with it.

guaranteed_improvement.why: There is no feature/label table to add to any baseline, so no condition for guaranteed improvement is met.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predicting Argonaute-nuclease cleavage activity from mutant protein sequence and guide/target mismatch position. The data needed for it exists only as gel photographs for ~37 constructs and 21 mismatch positions, so the project cannot start.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes I downloaded (30 MB Word supplement, 1.9 MB mmCIF); no modelling workload was estimated because no table exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the rows in the supplementary tables - 37 plasmids and 31 oligonucleotides, with no activity values at all. That took one command and killed it.

verdict_reason: A pure structural-mechanism paper: the only deposited data is one cryo-EM map (EMD-69324) and one atomic model (PDB 23WQ), and the supplement holds just sequences, plasmid names and collection statistics. Fails A2 (the prediction target exists only inside gel images and bar charts), A4 (no quantitative table, so no units) and A5 (37 mutant constructs, far under the ~400-row floor).
